key_insight: Constraint-aware reinforcement learning smooths PV output while reducing required battery power and energy capacity relative to conventional ramp-rate control.
engineering_relevance: Joint battery sizing and controller design can reduce storage requirements for grid-compliant PV integration; this work concerns system operation, not perovskite cell materials.
method: Learn a causal state-feedback policy from historical PV data without deployment-time forecasts.
Enforce ramp-rate, converter-power, and state-of-charge constraints through a causal feasibility interval.
Use full-horizon input-convex neural network optimization as a noncausal sizing benchmark.
evidence_signal: Across three real-world PV datasets at a 10%/min ramp-rate limit, CARL reduced peak battery power by 8.7–10.4% and energy capacity by 47.5–62.6% versus conventional ramp-rate control while maintaining grid-code compliance.
watch_item: Deployment should verify that the feasibility interval remains nonempty under extreme PV ramps and the selected battery power and energy limits.
paper_title: Battery Energy Storage Sizing in PV Ramp-Rate Smoothing using Constraint-Aware Reinforcement Learning-Based Controller
